subject: Clarify SOC 2 report cutoff vs point-in-time snapshot for customer evidence
messages:
From: KPMG SOC2 Team <soc2@kpmg.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Ocean Health Security <security@oceanhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: SOC 2 report cutoff: inclusive months vs point-in-time evidence

Hi Karthik,

We're preparing the SOC 2 Type II testing memo for Ocean Health Systems and need to confirm a few details about the period coverage and evidence artifacts. The report we received (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf) shows "Period: Jan 1, 2025 - Dec 31, 2025" but some of the customer reviewers are asking whether that means:

- The controls were tested "through" Dec 31, 2025 (i.e., inclusive of the full day and all end-of-day procedures), or
- Whether certain infrastructure artifacts are considered "point-in-time" (for example: AMI hashes, snapshot exports, and instance inventories captured at a single timestamp) and therefore represent evidence as-of a specific moment rather than continuous testing.

Specifically: Ocean Health is asking whether the infra snapshot you provided (infra-snapshot-2025-12-31.csv) is treated as evidence 'as of 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC' and whether any subsequent short-term changes (e.g., emergency patching on 2026-01-02) would fall outside the report period. They'd like an explicit statement on the report's boundary semantics and whether a bridge letter might be issued to cover any operational changes occurring in the short gap between the report cutoff and their procurement decision.

Can you confirm:
1) Whether the SOC 2 report's period is inclusive of the full date listed and how you treat end-of-day snapshots;
2) Whether Redwood can provide a short bridge letter (1 page) that attests to no material changes to described control families between 2025-12-31 and 2026-01-15, or alternatively provide a list of changes that would be considered material;
3) If point-in-time artifacts are considered supplemental (and how they're described) vs core evidence used for extent-of-testing.

Thanks,

Emma Liu
KPMG SOC2 Team
On behalf of Ocean Health Security

Attachment: sample-request-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: KPMG SOC2 Team <soc2@kpmg.com>, Ocean Health Security <security@oceanhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report cutoff: inclusive months vs point-in-time evidence

Emma / Ocean Health team,

Thanks for the clear questions — happy to clarify from Redwood's side. Short answers up front:

1) "Inclusive period" — Our SOC 2 Type II report period (Jan 1, 2025 - Dec 31, 2025) is inclusive: auditors test control operating effectiveness over that full interval. Point-in-time snapshots (AMI listings, infra CSVs) are used as supporting evidence to demonstrate configuration/state at specific checkpoints that correspond to testing activities during the period.

2) "Point-in-time vs continuous" — Point-in-time artifacts are supplemental evidence used to demonstrate that a control operating during the period produced the expected state at sample times. They are not the sole basis of opinion; the auditor's procedures and sampling determine extent of testing.

3) "Bridge letters" — We can provide a concise bridge letter covering the short gap (we normally do 30-day statements when requested). We can either: (A) attest to no material changes across control families between 2025-12-31 and a specified date (we prefer to limit to 30 days), or (B) provide a change log + risk description for any material updates.

Next steps: if Ocean Health would like a formal bridge letter we can draft it and route to KPMG for acceptance language. Marissa / Evelyn — can you confirm availability to produce the bridge letter and the most recent infra snapshot (AMI ids + instance inventory) for 2026-01-10 to support a Jan 15 bridge?

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (pdf, 4.2MB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, KPMG SOC2 Team <soc2@kpmg.com>, Ocean Health Security <security@oceanhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 15:28:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report cutoff: inclusive months vs point-in-time evidence

Karthik / all,

I can draft the bridge letter. To be explicit in wording we'll:
- State the report period is inclusive of Dec 31, 2025.
- Clarify that infra-snapshot-2025-12-31.csv represents evidence captured at 2025-12-31 23:59:59 UTC for auditor sampling and is supplemental to continuous control testing over the stated period.
- Offer a 30-day bridge attestation window (through 2026-01-30) attesting to no material changes to control families: Change Management, Logical Access, Backup & Restore, and Production Monitoring, except for routine non-material maintenance.

Evelyn — I need the following to finalize the bridge letter and the short change log:
- The validated infra snapshot for 2026-01-10 (AMI IDs, instance ids, region tags)
- A one-paragraph description for any maintenance events between 2025-12-31 and 2026-01-30 that touched production (if none, say so)
- Confirmation whether we want KPMG to include a line that the bridge letter is provided for procurement purposes only and not an expansion of the SOC opinion.

I'll prepare a draft and circulate for signature.

Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report cutoff: inclusive months vs point-in-time evidence

Marissa / Karthik / Emma (KPMG) —

I've attached the validated infra snapshot for 2026-01-10 and a short change log. Summary: between 2025-12-31 and 2026-01-30 we applied routine kernel patching to a small subset of non-customer-facing analytics hosts (no change to production inference fleet), rotated a pair of VPC peering keys (rotations logged), and completed one emergency patch on 2026-01-02 to an internal CI runner (no customer data exposure). None of these events are material to the control families tested for Ocean Health; we recommend the 30-day bridge attestation language be limited to procurement use.

Attachments included: infra-snapshot-2025-12-31.csv (csv), infra-snapshot-2026-01-10.csv (csv), change-log-2026-01-02-to-01-30.txt (txt)

Thanks — I'll send the draft bridge letter by end of day; Marissa, please advise if we should call out any of the rotations explicitly in the letter.

Evelyn Hart
